subject: Vendor onboarding: KYC evidence + PO attribute mapping mismatch
messages:
From: Claire Donovan <procurement@medicore.com>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Alan Cho <it-onboard@medicore.com>
Date: Sun, 31 Aug 2025 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Vendor onboarding: KYC evidence + PO attribute mapping mismatch

Hi Sean / Marissa,

Thanks again for the walkthrough last week. We're hitting two blockers on Medicore's side while trying to complete Ariba enrollment for Redwood:

1) KYC / evidence bundle: our procurement system requires a named evidence bundle (certificate of insurance + SOC attestation + org chart). The vendor portal flags the SOC item as "not accepted" because the PDF metadata doesn't show the expected issuer (we've attached the bundle).

2) PO attribute mismatch: our EDI/PO template expects a boolean field "po_ack_required" and a separate vendor_tax_id element at the header level. During ingestion the portal maps Redwood's order form "Tax ID" into a line-level attribute which fails our PO validation. Attached is the EDI template from our integration team.

We're paused on finalizing the MSA/order form because our downstream PO acceptance tests keep failing. Legal redlines you circulated changed the signature block and added conditional indemnity language; that also changed which party needs to provide tax fields in our system. We wanted to surface that in case there's a simple alignment option on your side.

Can we get:
- A short note from Redwood confirming whether you can expose vendor_tax_id at the PO header (or if we should parse it from a billing contact).
- A corrected SOC PDF (or metadata note) so our portal accepts the evidence bundle, or guidance on acceptable metadata.

Alan from our IT onboarding team is cc'd; he can ingest a new XML if you provide it.

Attachments: medicore_evidence_bundle.pdf (see SOC page), edi_po_template.xml

Thanks,
Claire Donovan
Senior Procurement Manager | Medicore Health
procurement@medicore.com

---

On a related note, if there are contract-level amendments required to keep your order form behavior predictable for us, flag them and we'll route to our legal team.

From: Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.com>
To: Claire Donovan <procurement@medicore.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>, Alan Cho <it-onboard@medicore.com>
Date: Mon, 1 Sep 2025 10:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Vendor onboarding: KYC evidence + PO attribute mapping mismatch

Claire — thanks for the clear note and the attachments.

Quick answers up front:
- We can surface vendor_tax_id at the PO header. That's a configuration change on our order form mapping (should be a painless tweak on Redwood's side).
- On the SOC PDF, we see the metadata issue you described — it's an export from our compliance silo that strips the issuer field. We'll re-export from our governance repo and return a corrected PDF with unambiguous issuer metadata by EOD tomorrow.

Kimberly — tagging you because Claire mentions the MSA redline and conditional indemnity. The change that went in was requested by the prospect during negotiation; if Medicore needs header-level tax obligations tied to liability language, legal will need to confirm the acceptable amendment approach. Can you advise if a short order form amendment (one paragraph) is acceptable vs a full MSA tweak?

Proposed mutual action plan:
- Tue 2 Sep: Redwood sends corrected SOC PDF and updated order form mapping (we'll provide the XML schema we will supply to Ariba).
- Wed 3 Sep: Medicore IT ingests test PO; if failure persists, we do a 30-min screen-share to trace the mapping.
- Fri 5 Sep: Target sign-off on onboarding checklist (we'll aim for this but will escalate if legal blocks remain).

Claire / Alan — cc'd Alan to confirm the ingestion endpoint details (callback URL and test account).

Thanks,
Sean Gallagher
Vendor Onboarding Lead | Redwood Inference
sean_gallagher@redwood.com
(415) 555-0189

From: Claire Donovan <procurement@medicore.com>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.com>
Cc: Alan Cho <it-onboard@medicore.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 2 Sep 2025 11:24:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Vendor onboarding: KYC evidence + PO attribute mapping mismatch

Thanks Sean — attaching the test artifacts we use on the Medicore side after your mapping change: edi_po_template.xml (shows header-level vendor_tax_id + po_ack_required boolean) and a small sample PO.

On the SOC PDF: we confirmed the portal expects an issuer name in PDF metadata matching one of our trusted authorities. If you can re-issue the SOC with issuer="SharedAudit" in the metadata or supply an attestation letter named explicitly, that should pass.

Alan notes the ingestion endpoint is: https://integration.medicore.com/po/test with basic auth; he'll share test credentials separately.

On the legal side, here's what our counsel prefers: if Redwood's redline changed liability/indemnity allocation materially (they flagged the addition of conditional indemnity tied to data residency), we'd prefer a short amendment to the order form referencing the original MSA rather than reopening the primary MSA. That keeps the signature path lighter.

Sample ask: an "Order Form Amendment" with two lines: (1) confirm vendor_tax_id will be emitted at header level and (2) accept conditional indemnity language limited to Medicore production data only. If Redwood legal agrees we can sign the amendment, and Alan can complete ingestion testing.

Attachments: edi_po_template.xml, sample_po_001.xml

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>

Date: Tue, 2 Sep 2025 16:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Vendor onboarding: KYC evidence + PO attribute mapping mismatch

Claire / team — thanks for the details and artifacts. I'm Kimberly on Redwood Legal. I reviewed the redline history and the proposed narrow amendment approach is acceptable to our legal team with a few edits.

Key points: 
- We can provide an "Order Form Amendment" (one page) that: (a) confirms Redwood will emit vendor_tax_id at the PO header for Medicore integrations, and (b) clarifies that the conditional indemnity language applies only to the processing of Medicore production data as defined in the amendment and does not broaden Redwood's MSA liability beyond that scope.
- We'll add a short acceptance clause that the amendment takes precedence over any conflicting order form fields for the purpose of EDI ingestion.

Deliverables & timeline: 
- I will draft the amendment and a clean order form exhibit by Wed 3 Sep COB PT.
- Sean / Marissa: please validate the order form exhibit contains the header mapping lines and the sample XML element names (vendor_tax_id, po_ack_required).
- Claire / Alan: please run ingestion once we send the amended exhibit; if false positives remain we can do a test session Thu 4 Sep.

Attachments: orderform_amendment_draft.docx (draft for internal review)

If that sounds workable I will route the amendment for signature via DocuSign and include the Medicore signatory block.

Best,
Kimberly Park
Senior Counsel | Redwood Inference
kimberly_park@redwood.com
